title: Janapada of Matsya
capsule: Matsya was one of the sixteen Mahājanapadas (great realms) of the 6th–4th centuries BCE, occupying northeastern Rajasthan between the Sarasvatī River and the Chambal hills, with its capital at Virāṭanagara (modern Bairāṭ near Jaipur). Its origins stretch to the Ṛgvedic Battle of the Ten Kings, where the Matsyas opposed King Sudās; the Aṅguttara Nikāya and Manu-Saṃhitā both place it within the sacred Brahmarṣi-deśa heartland. Unlike several neighboring Mahājanapadas that shifted to republican governance, Matsya maintained monarchical rule throughout its attested existence. The kingdom was eventually absorbed by the expanding Magadha empire, probably in the second half of the 4th century BCE.
